events.text: Picking up where The Seven Days ended: high above the finished world in golden light, the camera falls. Through cloud, over the river lands, down and down to bare dry ground, and on into a single grain of dust in extreme macro.
The fall from sky to ground: wind rush, a whoosh, then sudden silence on the grain of dust.
Silence. Dark damp dust in macro. A wind moves across it and the dust lifts. Hard cut: a man's eye opening, very close, first light in it (Adam, cast portrait). A first breath, loud in the silence.
The breath: a deep in-breath, the score's first swell under it, then cut to black.

Flash-forward montage, about one second a shot, the score driving: a river splitting into four from far above; gold glinting in a riverbed; two trees standing apart in soft light; a lion, an ibex, an eagle passing before the man; the man asleep under a tree at night; a woman's face in morning light (Eve, cast portrait); two hands meeting. Then black.
Montage at full drive, then the music cuts to nothing.

events.speaker: GOD
events.text: It is not good for the man to be alone.
Silence on black.

Night in the wilderness camp. Tents in rows under the stars, and at the centre of the camp a great tent sanctuary, its curtained gate facing east, fire and smoke rising before it. The brick-maker from The Seven Days, free now, sits at the door of his tent and watches it.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Seven times in chapter one, God looked at His world and called it good. In chapter two, for the first time, something is not good. And the people who first heard this lived in tents around a sanctuary. They would have noticed something about this garden. It looks like one.
THE GARDEN / Genesis 2:4 to 25
Title over dry ground at first light. Low hit, one swell, then quiet.
The wide world of The Seven Days from high above; then a slow descent to the ground, the camera coming to rest at the height of a man's eye on bare earth.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: This is the account of the heavens and the earth when they were created, in the day that the LORD God made them.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Listen to the turn inside the verse. The heavens and the earth become the earth and the heavens, and the camera comes down from the sky to the ground.
On screen, one word at a time over the film's own shots, each with a soft hit: forms, breathes, plants, takes, places, commands, brings, closes, builds.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: And God now has a name. The LORD, in small capitals, stands for His covenant name. In chapter one He speaks and worlds appear. Here He stoops and works with His hands. He forms, breathes, plants, takes, places, commands, brings, closes and builds.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: This is not a second, competing creation story. It is a close up of the sixth day, and Jesus quotes both chapters together as one word from the Creator.
Bare dry ground at first light. No shrub, no plant, no cloud. Then springs well up from below and the water spreads, darkening the dust in long slow ribbons.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: Now no shrub of the field had yet appeared on the earth, nor had any plant of the field sprouted, for the LORD God had not yet sent rain upon the earth, and there was no man to cultivate the ground.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: But springs welled up from the earth and watered the whole surface of the ground.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: The scene opens with what is missing. No shrub, no plant, no rain, and no man to cultivate the ground. Every lack is about to be met.
Silence. Water ticking into the dust.

Set piece: the forming. The damp dust stirs and gathers, drawn together by wind and light into the shape of a man lying on the ground, seen from far off; nothing else moves. No hands, no figure: only the effect. Then a wind passes over him, low and close, the grass bending. His chest rises. His eyes open.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: Then the LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground and breathed the breath of life into his nostrils, and the man became a living being.
Set piece: the breath. The film's first peak, warm and immense, no narration: the man's first breaths, his hand closing on the earth, first light across his face.
The wilderness camp by day: the brick-maker kneels and lets dry dust run through fingers that once shaped bricks in Egypt.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Formed is the potter's verb, the word for hands shaping clay. Isaiah says it plainly:

events.speaker: READER
events.text: we are the clay, and You are the potter,

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: The nations also told of humans made from clay, as servants to spare the gods their labour. Genesis is different. This man is given a garden, good food and meaningful work, and God's own breath.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Man, adam, is taken from the ground, adamah. We are earthy creatures, given dignity only by the breath of God.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: the breath of the Almighty gives me life,

Two to three second cuts, the score rising: shoots breaking the ground, trees climbing toward the light, fruit swelling on the branch: figs, pomegranates, dates, grapes, olives. Then wide: a garden planted in the east, and at its centre two trees standing apart in soft light.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: And the LORD God planted a garden in Eden, in the east, where He placed the man He had formed.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: Out of the ground the LORD God gave growth to every tree that is pleasing to the eye and good for food. And in the middle of the garden were the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Eden means delight. It is a garden of God's own planting, the first place where God dwells with man.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Notice the two trees in the middle. They are placed carefully, with the man, the woman and the command, so that the next chapter can test each one.

Set piece: the river. Following one river out of the garden from just above the water, faster and faster, until it breaks into four great headwaters and the camera climbs to see all four running out across the land.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: Now a river flowed out of Eden to water the garden, and from there it branched into four headwaters:

Each river in turn from the air, its name on screen: the Pishon winding through a land of gold, gold glinting in the riverbed, pale resin and dark banded stone in the shallows; the Gihon through the far south; the Tigris; the Euphrates.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: The name of the first river is the Pishon; it winds through the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: And the gold of that land is pure, and bdellium and onyx are found there.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: The name of the second river is the Gihon; it winds through the whole land of Cush.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: The name of the third river is the Tigris; it runs along the east side of Assyria. And the fourth river is the Euphrates.
Set piece: the four rivers, from far above. The second peak, no narration; the score above where the voice sat.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: The geography is deliberately real and deliberately beyond reach. Every Israelite knew the Tigris and the Euphrates. The Pishon and the Gihon cannot be identified with certainty.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: And in the ancient world, the dwelling of a god was a place of abundant water. Here a river flows out from the place where God dwells, to water the whole world.
Hard cut to the wilderness camp.

The wilderness camp at sunrise. The brick-maker walks toward the great tent at its centre. Its gate faces east into the rising sun. Inside the court, gold catches the light. A priest stands at the gate, two dark onyx stones set on his shoulders, engraved with names. Woven into the inner curtains, cherubim among palms and open flowers.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Now look at the camp the first hearers lived in.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: For Israel, the garden looked like a sanctuary. Its entrance faces east, as the tabernacle's did. Gold and onyx were the materials of the priestly garments, and two onyx stones, engraved with the tribes' names, sat on the high priest's shoulders.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: In the next chapter God walks in the garden, the same form of the verb He uses when He promises Israel:

events.speaker: READER
events.text: I will walk among you and be your God,

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Israel's worship was, in part, a memory of Eden.

The man at work among the trees of the garden at first light, turning the soil, tending a vine. Match cut: a Levite at the sanctuary, tending the court in the same light; then standing guard at its gate.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: Then the LORD God took the man and placed him in the Garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Cultivate and keep. The first verb means to work or serve, and is the ordinary word for serving God in worship. The second means to guard and keep, the word for keeping God's commands.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Together they describe the Levites in the tabernacle. Adam's work is farming, but it is also priestly service in the place where God dwells.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: A keeper of a sanctuary needs one more thing. A word from the One who lives there.

Stillness in the middle of the garden. The tree of the knowledge of good and evil, heavy with fruit. No figure: only a wind that moves softly through every leaf at once. The man stands before it, small.
The wind through the leaves; everything else falls silent.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: And the LORD God commanded him,

events.speaker: GOD
events.text: “You may eat freely from every tree of the garden,

events.speaker: GOD
events.text: but you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil; for in the day that you eat of it, you will surely die.”
Hold on the tree after the warning. Silence.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Listen to the order. The command opens with permission, every tree of the garden, and only then sets one limit. God's commands are not the grudging rules of a jealous master, but the boundaries of a good home.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: And the warning is plain. God does not hide the consequences of disobedience. His word defines what is good and what is evil, and life depends on trusting it.
Pause on the tree, heavy with fruit, the wind in its leaves.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Whatever the knowledge of good and evil means exactly, the heart of the matter is trust: whether the man will receive it from God's word, or seize it on his own terms.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: So the garden has everything. Food, beauty, work, and a word to live by. And then God Himself says that something is missing.
Evening. The man alone in the wide garden, very small among the trees, the light going.
Wind; a single bird far off; the music gone.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: The LORD God also said,

events.speaker: GOD
events.text: “It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make for him a suitable helper.”

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: The first thing in the Bible called not good. And it is God Himself who names the lack, before the man does.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Helper is ezer, and Scripture uses that word most often of God Himself.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: My help comes from the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: It speaks of strength brought alongside, never of someone lesser. Suitable means one who stands face to face with him, his match.

Montage, two to three second cuts, the score driving: the beasts of the field and the birds of the air coming before the man one by one: a lion, a herd of gazelle, an ibex on the rocks, a bear, an eagle settling on a branch, a pair of doves. He looks at each and speaks. Then they pass, and he is alone again.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: And out of the ground the LORD God formed every beast of the field and every bird of the air, and He brought them to the man to see what he would name each one. And whatever the man called each living creature, that was its name.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: The man gave names to all the livestock, to the birds of the air, and to every beast of the field. But for Adam no suitable helper was found.
The last animal turns away. The music stops on the man alone.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: God brings the animals to the man to see what he would name each one, and honours his choices. But none of them stands face to face with him.
Dusk deepening into night over the garden; the man asleep beneath a tree, seen from far away; stars; soft light gathering near him. No figure.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: So the LORD God caused the man to fall into a deep sleep, and while he slept, He took one of the man’s ribs and closed up the area with flesh.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: And from the rib that the LORD God had taken from the man, He made a woman and brought her to him.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: The deep sleep is the same sleep that falls on Abram before God makes covenant with him. God works while the man is passive.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Rib can mean side, a builder's word used of the tabernacle's sides. And made is literally built. God builds the woman as a builder raises a house, and then He Himself brings her to the man.

Set piece: the woman brought to the man. Morning light through the garden. She walks toward him through the trees (Eve, cast portrait, framed head and shoulders, long hair). He wakes, rises and turns. His face as he sees her. Face to face.
Set piece: the third peak, the warmest in the film, no narration; then the music falls away for his words.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: And the man said: “This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called ‘woman,’ for out of man she was taken.”
Hold on the two faces. Silence.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: These are the first recorded human words in the Bible, and they are poetry. Man and woman, ish and ishshah, sound alike. Bone of my bones is the language of family.
The wilderness camp at evening: the brick-maker and his wife at the door of their tent, their children asleep inside, the sanctuary's fire beyond.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and they will become one flesh.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: The narrator steps out of the story to apply it to every marriage after it. To be united is to cling or hold fast, the word Ruth uses of Naomi, and the word Moses uses of Israel and God:

events.speaker: READER
events.text: Hold fast to Him,

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Marriage is a loyalty chosen and kept, not only a feeling. This chapter was written to shape Israel's homes.
The garden in full light, the two far off together among the trees; peace, no fear.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: And the man and his wife were both naked, and they were not ashamed.
Hold. Then the wind stirs the grass at the foot of the tree in the middle of the garden. The music turns.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Naked, and not ashamed. The line closes the scene and sets up the next one. Every gift in this chapter is about to be tested.
Light falling into a garden at dawn: an olive grove at night with torches moving through it; then a rock cut tomb in a garden, its stone rolled back, no figures.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Paul quotes this chapter and names Jesus as the last Adam.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: The first man Adam became a living being; the last Adam a life-giving spirit,

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: Adam was placed in a garden to serve and guard it, and given one word to keep. He failed at every point. Christ comes as the obedient Man who serves His Father perfectly.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: John frames the passion with gardens. Jesus is arrested in a garden, buried in a garden, and on Easter morning Mary thinks He is the gardener. In a sense she is right.
Set piece: the empty tomb in the garden at sunrise, light on the path. The same wind that passed over the dust in Eden moves through the garden. No narration.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: That evening He breathes on His disciples, as God breathed into the first man, and says:

events.speaker: READER
events.text: Receive the Holy Spirit,

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: And Paul says the one flesh union was always pointing beyond itself.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: This mystery is profound, but I am speaking about Christ and the church,

Flash-forward, dark and fast: thorns breaking the soil; a man's hands bleeding on hard ground; a flaming sword turning before the way to the tree. Then the wilderness camp: the brick-maker looking out over desert.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: When chapter three comes, each gift in this garden is damaged. The ground is cursed, work becomes toil, the marriage is strained, shame replaces nakedness without shame, and the way to the tree of life is barred.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: But the prophets kept the garden alive. They promised a people in the desert that God

events.speaker: READER
events.text: will make her wilderness like Eden and her desert like the garden of the LORD,
Set piece: Eden restored. A radiant city with a river of clear water running through its centre, and the tree of life on both banks, fruit hanging in the light.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: And the Bible ends with Eden restored and surpassed. The river of the water of life flows from the throne of God and of the Lamb, and the tree of life stands on either side of it.

events.speaker: READER
events.text: eat from the tree of life in the Paradise of God,
Set piece: Eden restored. The fourth peak, radiant, no narration.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: The garden has become a city, but it is still a home where God and His people live together.
Back to the first image: dust on the ground, a breath of wind, first light.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: We are dust that breathes because He breathed. Every good gift, food, work, beauty, marriage and friendship, comes from His hand, and even His limits are a form of His care.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: You were formed from dust and given life by God's breath. How does remembering that change how you see your worth today?
Hold on the light.
The tree in the middle of the garden at dusk. Something moves in the grass at its foot, unseen. Cut to black.

events.speaker: GUIDE
events.text: One tree, one word, and a man and a woman who trust it. In the next chapter, another voice speaks in the garden, and the first question it asks is about what God said.

End card with a WATCH NEXT space for The Fall.
